input.explanation: Compound interest means you earn interest every year, and it's calculated only on the money you first put in. If I put 100 and the rate is 10%, I get 10 each year, so after 3 years I have 130. It grows faster than saving without interest.

analysis.praise: You know that interest is earned over time and that saving with interest beats saving without it.

concepts.label: Interest is earned over time
concepts.expected_idea: Interest is a percentage paid on money kept in an account.

concepts.label: Interest is charged on the growing balance
concepts.expected_idea: In compound interest, each year's interest is calculated on the original amount plus interest already earned.
concepts.evidence_quote: it's calculated only on the money you first put in
concepts.reason: Interest only on the original amount is simple interest, which is a different thing.

concepts.label: Growth speeds up over time
concepts.expected_idea: Because the balance grows, each year's gain is larger than the last, which is exponential growth.
concepts.reason: You didn't say that the yearly gains themselves grow.

concepts.label: Compounding beats no interest
concepts.expected_idea: Interest makes savings grow, and compounding makes them grow faster than simple interest.
concepts.evidence_quote: It grows faster than saving without interest.
concepts.reason: True, but the comparison that matters is with simple interest.

concepts.label: Computing the balance
concepts.reason: 130 is the simple-interest result; compounding gives 133.10.

lessons.title: Interest earns interest
lessons.core_idea: In compound interest, each period's interest is added to the balance, and the next interest is calculated on that bigger balance. Interest calculated only on the original deposit is called simple interest.
lessons.example: 100 at 10%: year 1 interest is 10, so the balance is 110. In year 2 the interest is 10% of 110, which is 11, not 10.
lessons.you_said: Interest is only calculated on the money you first put in.
lessons.actually: It is calculated on the deposit plus the interest already earned.
lessons.check_yourself: In year 2, what is the 10% applied to?

lessons.title: Multiply by 1.1 each year
lessons.core_idea: Growing by 10% means multiplying by 1.10. After 3 years: 100 × 1.1 × 1.1 × 1.1 = 133.10, not 130.
lessons.example: 130 is what simple interest gives; the extra 3.10 is interest earned on interest.
lessons.check_yourself: What is 100 worth after 2 years at 10% compounded?

lessons.title: Why growth speeds up
lessons.core_idea: Each year's interest is calculated on a larger balance, so the yearly gains themselves grow: 10, 11, 12.10 and so on. The curve bends upward, which is called exponential growth.
lessons.example: A snowball rolling downhill picks up more snow on each turn because it is bigger.
lessons.you_said: You didn't mention that the gains grow over time.
lessons.actually: The yearly gain increases because the balance it is calculated on increases.
lessons.check_yourself: Which year's interest is larger, year 1 or year 5?

questions.prompt: You deposit 200 at 5% yearly interest, compounded annually. In year 2, the interest is calculated on…
options: The 200 plus the interest earned in year 1
Only the interest earned in year 1
The average of the two balances

questions.prompt: What is the balance after 2 years on 1000 at 10% compounded annually? Show your steps.

rubric.full_credit: After year 1 it is 1100; year 2 interest is 110, so 1210.
rubric.partial_credit: Gets 1100 for year 1 but not 1210 for year 2.

questions.prompt: Why does a compound-interest balance grow by larger amounts each year, even though the rate stays the same?

rubric.full_credit: Because each year the interest is calculated on a bigger balance that includes earlier interest.
rubric.partial_credit: Says the balance gets bigger without linking it to interest being calculated on it.

sample_answers.Q2: After year 1 it is 1100. In year 2 the interest is 10% of 1100, which is 110, so I have 1210.
sample_answers.Q3: Because the balance gets bigger every year.

Q2.feedback: Exactly right: 1100 after year 1, then 10% of 1100 is 110, giving 1210.
